findings.title: res.json() in balanceFetcher returns any — BalanceData type annotation is not enforced at runtime
findings.description: res.json() returns Promise<any>. The function's declared return type Promise<BalanceData> satisfies the TypeScript checker structurally but provides no runtime enforcement. If the API returns a malformed response (e.g., balance as null, a string, or missing entirely), the caller receives a value that does not match BalanceData but TypeScript reports no error. This is the upstream cause of the NaN-sliderMax risk in TradePanel. A runtime validator (zod.parse or a manual shape check) is needed at this boundary.

findings.title: commitInput does not guard against NaN sliderMax — setAmount(NaN) can propagate silently
findings.description: commitInput guards the user-typed value with isNaN(parsed) ? 1 : parsed (line 81), but it does not guard sliderMax. sliderMax = balance, and balance derives from balanceData?.balance which is unvalidated (see balance-fetcher finding). If balanceData.balance is NaN or non-numeric, sliderMax is NaN. Math.min(Math.max(valid, 1), NaN) returns NaN. The comparison clamped < valid is false for NaN so flashBalanceError never fires. setAmount(NaN) is called, and NaN propagates into sharesForCost, priceImpact, and the buy-button label. The fix at the fetcher boundary (runtime validation) is the preferred solution, but a local guard here also helps defensively.

findings.title: checkStaleness accesses fresh.* fields on implicit any — no type coverage for market API response
findings.description: const fresh = await res.json() on line 123 infers as any. Subsequent accesses — fresh.priceYes, fresh.priceNo, fresh.quantityYes, fresh.quantityNo, fresh.bParameter — are all untyped. TypeScript cannot catch a field rename or API shape change here. The staleness check could silently pass (outcomeDelta = NaN, NaN > 0.02 is false) or silently pass wrong data to sharesForCost if the API response structure changes.

findings.title: trackRef.current! non-null assertion in valueFromPointer — logically safe but suppresses the null checker
findings.description: trackRef.current! is used inside valueFromPointer, which is only called from handlePointerDown and handlePointerMove. Both handlers are attached to the same <div> that holds the ref, so the element cannot be unmounted while actively dispatching to itself — the assertion is safe in practice. However, it permanently silences the null checker for this access. If valueFromPointer were ever called from a different context (e.g., a keyboard handler or an effect) the assertion would be wrong and would produce a runtime crash rather than a compile-time error. A type guard is more future-proof.

residual_risks: lastLoginReward: string | null in BalanceData is plausible but unverified at runtime — if the API changes this field (e.g., to a Date string or drops it), consumers will receive undefined with no TypeScript error due to the unvalidated res.json() cast.

The userBalance?: number optional prop with nullish coalescing is safe for the 0-balance edge case (0 ?? 500 = 0, correct). However, when sliderMax=0 the slider renders with min=1 and max=0, which means CoinSlider passes an inverted range to Math.round(ratio * max) — the slider ball will always render at ballPct=0 and snap points will all resolve to 0 via Math.max(1, Math.round(pct*0))=1. This is a UX edge case rather than a type error, but it is worth verifying with a zero-balance test user.

ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> on line 54 of TradePanel.tsx is correct and idiomatic for a use-client component — no issue. When @types/node is installed, this resolves to NodeJS.Timeout, and clearTimeout accepts that type without complaint.
testing_gaps: No test covers the path where /api/balance returns a non-numeric or missing balance field — the NaN propagation through commitInput and the LMSR calculations would only surface in production.
No test covers checkStaleness with a malformed /api/markets/:id response — the any-typed fresh object means a field rename would pass all static checks and only fail at runtime.
The sliderMax=0 scenario (user with 0 balance) has no visible test coverage — CoinSlider behavior with min > max is untested.
